title: Case #4: The Leaked Build
summary: An unreleased Starfall Arena build is on a public forum. Its watermark says which one; the org chart says who shouldn't have had it.

steps.title: Case #4
body: Saturday night, a data-mining forum posts an unreleased build of *Starfall Arena*: new maps, new heroes, the whole season spoiled. Vera Okonkwo, the CEO, calls Rosa at midnight.

Every Pixelforge build carries an invisible **watermark**. The leak report has it. Access to pre-release builds is logged, and only **Marcus Bell's engineering organisation** (which includes QA) is cleared to download them.
Tables: `employees`, `builds`, `leak_report`, `build_access`, `uploads`. Use subqueries and CTEs: no guessing ids by eye.

steps.title: Clue 1: which build?
prompt: Return the **name** and **size_mb** of the build whose watermark matches the one in `leak_report`. Use a subquery, not a hard-coded watermark.

steps.title: Clue 2: who touched it?
prompt: Return the **name** and **team** of everyone who accessed that build. Find the build with a subquery again.

Tables: `employees(id, name, title, team, manager_id, salary)`, `builds(id, name, watermark, size_mb)`, `leak_report(id, forum, posted_at, watermark)`, `build_access(id, employee_id, build_id, accessed_at)`, `uploads(id, employee_id, at, size_mb, destination)`.
solution: WHERE build_id = (SELECT id FROM builds WHERE watermark = (SELECT watermark FROM leak_report))

steps.title: Clue 3: outside the circle
prompt: Use a **recursive CTE** to collect everyone in Marcus Bell's organisation (Marcus included). Then return the **name** and **title** of everyone who accessed the leaked build but is **not** in that organisation.

Tables: `employees(id, name, title, team, manager_id, salary)`, `builds(id, name, watermark, size_mb)`, `leak_report(id, forum, posted_at, watermark)`, `build_access(id, employee_id, build_id, accessed_at)`, `uploads(id, employee_id, at, size_mb, destination)`.
solution: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE name = 'Marcus Bell'
SELECT e.id FROM employees AS e JOIN cleared AS c ON e.manager_id = c.id
SELECT id FROM builds WHERE watermark = (SELECT watermark FROM leak_report)
WHERE e.id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM build_access WHERE build_id = (SELECT id FROM leaked))
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cleared AS c WHERE c.id = e.id);

steps.title: Name the culprit
prompt: A copy of a build is the same size as the build. Return the **name** of the uncleared person who made an **upload of exactly the leaked build's size** **after** they accessed it.

Tables: `employees(id, name, title, team, manager_id, salary)`, `builds(id, name, watermark, size_mb)`, `leak_report(id, forum, posted_at, watermark)`, `build_access(id, employee_id, build_id, accessed_at)`, `uploads(id, employee_id, at, size_mb, destination)`.
solution: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE name = 'Marcus Bell'
SELECT e.id FROM employees AS e JOIN cleared AS c ON e.manager_id = c.id
SELECT id, size_mb FROM builds WHERE watermark = (SELECT watermark FROM leak_report)
JOIN build_access AS a ON a.employee_id = e.id AND a.build_id = (SELECT id FROM leaked)
WHERE e.id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM cleared)
